properties.title: Setting up a Security Token Service

body.h1: Setting up a Security Token Service
body.h3: Setting up a Security Token Service
body.p: Security Token Service can be set up as per WS-Trust specification using Rampart. The default security token service shipped with the rampart distribution is contained in the rampart-trust.mar module. It can issue SCT tokens and SAML tokens. Sample05 contains a client that connects to the default STS and obtain a SAML token. The services.xml in the sample contains "saml-issuer-config" parameter that is used to configure the default SAML issuer.

The default SAML issuers put the authenticated principal into the assertion's subject, as a saml:NameIdentifier (SAML 1.1) or a saml2:NameID (SAML 2.0), using the email address format. To choose the value or the Format yourself, or to add attributes, register a class implementing org.apache.rahas.impl.util.SAMLCallbackHandler in the saml-issuer-config:

The handler receives a SAMLNameIdentifierCallback for the subject and a SAMLAttributeCallback for the attribute statement; check getCallbackType() and ignore the ones you do not handle. For a SAML 2.0 assertion set the NameID with setSAML2NameID(); for SAML 1.1 use setNameId(). The default is used when the handler leaves it unset.

Nothing has to be removed from the modules directory. The default STS is the RequestSecurityToken operation that the rahas module adds to every service it is engaged to, so a service with its own issuer simply does not engage rahas. Write your own issuer implementing the "org.apache.rahas.TokenIssuer" interface. Let's say that your issuer is "org.custom.MyIssuer". Then create an Axis2 service archive with the following in the services.xml. The issuer class can be packaged inside the service archive: issuers, validators, renewers and cancelers are loaded with the service's class loader. Drop the archive into the repository and you have a STS with a custom token issuer.
body.pre:
<module ref="rampart" />
<operation name="IssueToken" mep="http://www.w3.org/ns/wsdl/in-out"> <messageReceiver class="org.apache.rahas.STSMessageReceiver"/>
<!-- Action mapping to accept RST requests --> <actionMapping>http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/02/trust/RST/SCT</actionMapping> <actionMapping>http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/02/trust/RST/Issue</actionMapping> <actionMapping>http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/02/trust/RST/Renew</actionMapping> <actionMapping>http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/02/trust/RST/Cancel</actionMapping> <actionMapping>http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/02/trust/RST/SCT/Cancel</actionMapping> <actionMapping>http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/02/trust/RST/Validate</actionMapping>
<parameter name="token-dispatcher-configuration"> <token-dispatcher-configuration> <!-- Issuers. You may have many issuers. --> <issuer class="org.custom.MyIssuer" default="true"> <configuration type="parameter">saml-issuer-config</configuration> <tokenType>http://docs.oasis-open.org/wss/oasis-wss-saml-token-profile-1.1#SAMLV1.1</tokenType> </issuer> </token-dispatcher-configuration> </parameter>
</operation>
